journey:sutherland-christ-in-glory.t: Christ in Glory in the Tetramorph
journey:sutherland-christ-in-glory.a: Graham Sutherland (design); woven by Pinton Frères
journey:sutherland-christ-in-glory.c: Felletin, France (woven); designed in England and France

x.summary: Behind the high altar of the new Coventry Cathedral, built beside the ruins of the medieval cathedral destroyed by bombing in 1940, Christ sits enthroned in a vast green field. He is enclosed in a mandorla and surrounded by the four living creatures of the Apocalypse that stand for the Evangelists. Below him, Sutherland placed a small Crucifixion, joining the Christ of the Passion to the Christ of glory in a single image of hope after war.
facts: At about 23 by 12 metres, it was one of the largest tapestries in the world when it was made.
A life-size human figure stands between Christ's feet, showing how huge the enthroned Christ is.
It was woven in a single piece by the Pinton workshop in Felletin, near Aubusson, and was installed for the cathedral's consecration in May 1962.
